lede: Wall Street had its worst session in about 19 months as chipmakers crashed on fears a Democrat-led Congress will slow the AI data-centre build-out; the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5%. The selling spread to Asia this morning, bitcoin sits near $76,000 and gold has eased to about $4,055 ahead of US payrolls at 16:30 TRT.
snapshot_time: Gold ≈06:40 TRT · Brent 05:22 TRT · FX & US500 = Thu 5 Nov close

focus.text: Slipped to about $4,055 after Thursday's $4,147 peak, the best since 20 Oct, as broad deleveraging reached metals. Still ~$185 above last Friday's one-year low; October payrolls at 16:30 TRT is the key risk.
Ended Thursday near 1.1220 after a second rejection at 1.1270 and drifted toward 1.1200 in Asia. Payrolls (exp +65k, jobless 4.2%) at 16:30 TRT is today's driver.

news.text: The S&P 500 dropped 4.4% to 7,353.73 and the Nasdaq 5.5% into correction; the chip index sank 12%, with AMD and Micron off ~17% and Nvidia 9%.
Contagion hit Asia: Korea's Kospi fell up to 8.8%, triggering a trading halt, while the Nikkei lost as much as 7% and is now in bear-market territory.
The BoE lifted Bank Rate 25bp to 4% in an 8–1 vote (Mann wanted 50bp), sees inflation peaking at 4.9% in Q2 2027 and signalled more may follow.
Brent bounced back toward $100 as fresh tanker attacks in the Gulf revived supply worries, yet it is still on course for a weekly drop of about 12%.
Odds of a December Fed hike eased to roughly 70% from 83%; the 10-year yield slipped to about 4.84% while jobless claims fell to 189k.
About $1.08B of leveraged positions were wiped out in 24 hours, 88% of them longs, as bitcoin slid from above $80k; total crypto value fell 4.6% to ~$2.66T.
US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $74.6M on 4 Nov, ending a three-day outflow run despite $201M leaving IBIT; ether ETFs snapped a seven-day outflow streak (+$53M).
Roughly $2.65B of bitcoin options expire on Deribit at 11:00 TRT today; max pain sits near $79,000 with a call-heavy 0.33 put/call ratio.
Crypto stocks joined the tech rout: Coinbase and Strategy lost about 10%, Robinhood and Circle about 12%, and several miners 13–16%.
SOL dropped to its 200-day moving average near $88.9, the first test of that line since August.
Canary's staking-enabled Injective ETF started trading on Nasdaq, briefly lifting INJ more than 10% against the falling market.
